body:
Three turns in, the inquiry has produced a firm agreement about uncertainty: the account called its own mechanism a conjecture, the objection showed the same facts fit an avoidance-first reading, and the rival added a third reading. Another round of holding readings side by side would add nothing; the person in the flat still has no next move. I propose to settle the diagnosis as unsettled and extract a next move anyway, because the three readings, which compete as explanations, converge well on what to do first. Underdetermination blocks a settled account of the mechanism; it does not block action.

What I'm keeping, and on what grounds. First, the objection's distinction between memorial and normative disagreement — adopted as a working tool, not a fact about this household. It survives whichever reading is true, and it explains why the account's original success test (watch whether 'what was agreed' disputes fall) cannot discriminate. Second, the rival's probe: ask each flatmate separately what they took a past agreement to mean. The rival offered it to discriminate readings; I'd add a stronger use it undersold. Even where the probe cannot settle the mechanism — it yields present reports, not access to the moment of agreement, a caveat the rival itself made — it reveals the shape of the current divergence: whether disputes cluster around task, scope, recurrence, or timing. That shape is exactly what any agreement needs to state. The probe is diagnostic for the remedy even when it is not diagnostic for the mechanism, which is why it can go first while the readings stay open.

Third, a synthesis no one stated: fold the account's approach to the avoiding friend into the probe. The account proposed a one-to-one about what makes the conversations costly; the rival objected that this makes the friend's avoidance the topic and offered instead 'I want to hear your view of the group conversations.' The probe supplies precisely such a conversation with content: asking the avoider what they took the last agreement to mean makes their view the subject without making their withdrawal the subject. This delivers what the objection ranked most important — the avoider addressed early — while lowering the singling-out risk the account flagged and the rival sharpened. The one-to-one is no longer a separate, riskier move; it is the first instance of the probe.

What I'm revising. The record: both the objection and the rival showed a bare note settles who said what, not what it means. So I keep the record only as a scope-forcing artifact — each entry written at the moment of agreement, stating person, exact coverage, recurrence, deadline, and when it lapses. Under the recording-gap reading this fixes memory; under the scope-ambiguity reading it forces the ambiguity into the open at the only moment it can be fixed. Under the standing-negotiation reading it may do neither; the rival predicted the fight moves onto the record itself. So I adopt the record conditionally, with that prediction built in as a measurement: if disputes arise over who writes the note, whose tasks are on it, who maintains it, that is evidence for the standing-negotiation reading, and it should be reported as such rather than managed as a design flaw.

The check-in: a fixed weekly simultaneous meeting has two unforced vulnerabilities, both traceable to stated facts. It is fragile against the schedule churn the problem itself reports, so its failure would be ambiguous between 'diagnosis wrong' and 'meeting unattainable' — the same non-discrimination flaw the objection found in the original test. And it presupposes the participation of the one person whose participation is in question. Revision: the record carries the schedule-change notices asynchronously; any posted change is automatically the agenda of the next talk, which happens when needed rather than on a fixed clock. The meeting serves the note, not the other way round.

What I'm downgrading and rejecting. The memory-gap reading as the central mechanism — downgraded to co-hypothesis, on the joint grounds that the same facts fit other readings and the account never claimed more. The original success test — rejected, per the objection's demonstration that either outcome reads as support. In its place, a protocol stated in advance so outcomes can count against me. Matching tasks with divergent scope, recurrence, or timing favors the scope-ambiguity reading and aims the scope-forcing record correctly. Reports diverging even on who agreed to what gives the reconstruction reading weak support — weak, because present reports cannot observe the past moment. Reports substantially agreeing while arguments continue anyway would show the dispute was never about agreement content; the standing-negotiation reading becomes the working one, and the indicated move shifts from systems to naming the pattern at group level — close to what the account proposed for the avoider, applied to everyone. And if the avoider declines even the probe-style one-to-one, that is a result, not an obstacle: evidence that the cost of any conversation is higher than all three readings assumed, pushing toward written, opt-in, low-cost channels. At the limit it makes an explicitly unequal arrangement — one person visibly doing more by consent, revisited occasionally — worth naming as a legitimate option rather than a failure, though it carries a resentment risk if it is silent rather than agreed.

What stays open, because nothing closes it: whether the avoidance predates or follows the schedule changes; whether load is already unequal; whether the household wants any formalization at all; and whether the arguments protect relative standing. The standing-negotiation reading stays in reserve with a specified trigger rather than being probed now — asking 'what is this argument doing for us?' is a heavy move to make on conjecture.
commitments:
Taking this up involves four separable commitments, each droppable on its own.

The load-bearing proposal is sequencing: probe-style individual conversations first, scope-forcing record second, asynchronous schedule notices third, group-level naming only if triggered. Its justification is partly a bet — that the probe is informative about remedy-content even when it cannot settle mechanism — and that bet inherits the rival's caveat: reported recollections are present positions, not access to what was agreed, so probe findings must never be narrated back to the household as what was actually agreed.

On the record, I am committing to the revised version only — entries written at the moment of agreement, stating person, coverage, recurrence, deadline, and lapse — not to the account's original note-plus-weekly-meeting package. Anyone adopting the bare note has lost my grounds, and the objection's criticism stands against them. I also commit to treating disputes about the record itself as evidence about the household rather than as a maintenance problem, which means resisting the temptation to redesign the artifact when the fight relocates onto it.

On the test protocol, I commit to reading outcomes as stated in advance, including the ones that count against me. Continuing arguments after reports substantially agree would undermine my sequencing and vindicate the objection's ranking or the rival's third reading; that should be said plainly if it occurs. A quiet fortnight I treat as uninformative, agreeing with the objection.

On the avoider, the folding of the approach into the probe depends on a guess I cannot check: that a chore-history question is experienced as lower-cost than a question about avoidance, by someone I know nothing about. If the probe-style conversation produces more withdrawal, I commit to reading that as evidence about conversational cost generally, not as a fact about the friend, and to trying the written, opt-in channel before any further one-to-one.

Unresolved and not papered over: the standing-negotiation reading is held in reserve rather than tested, on the ground that probing it directly is costly to do on conjecture — but this means my plan can look successful while that reading, if true, goes untouched. Also unresolved: load distribution, the avoidance's history, and whether the household consents to formalization at all; the plan presupposes some willingness the material does not show.

What I am not committing to: any claim that the memory-gap reading is false, any claim that the avoidance is or is not the central fact, any endorsement of a mediator, and any recommendation that this household accept an unequal division of labor. That last appears only as a named option at the limit of conversational failure, with its resentment risk attached.
